chapter: Clarinet fingering and the Tio family
title: Working a day trade and playing all night
summary: He recalls roofing by day, playing until three or four in the morning, and transposing piano copies into parts.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: That was the Spanish fort in those days. It was right at the lake. Yeah, they stayed out there about 35 years.

On the same job. Night after night. No days off. Yeah, it's hard. Shut up. You shut up all that time. But, you know, some of us get a kick out of it. Like I used to do. I didn't feel like I was working or anything. I used to get my kick out of it.

I'd get right up next morning and go to work. Go work at my trade all day. Sure. And play all night. Play all night. Go work at my trade all day. Play until 3, 4 o'clock in the morning. Get home, get an hour, two hours, sleep and go on again. I'd come home from work and eat. I'd eat. Get my bat and stuff. And I'd get in the bed. And I'd sleep till 8 o'clock. 9 o'clock. I was back on the job again.
That's pretty good. Keep that up.

And then I used to come in and sit down. Some nights I'd sit down and write, transpose, transpose from the piano copies. We wanted a number and we couldn't get the orchestration right away so we'd buy a piano copy. And I'd sit down and transpose parts off the piano copy, off the piano square.
